title: Testimony already borne is recorded in heaven
setting: Joseph Smith and his companions were traveling home from Independence to Ohio in August 1831. On 13 August they crossed the Missouri River at Chariton, Missouri. There they met Hyrum Smith, John Murdock, David Whitmer, and Harvey Whitlock, still headed to Zion. Murdock had been ill, and he and Hyrum had stayed in Chariton while he recovered. After a joyful meeting, Joseph Smith dictated this revelation on the riverbank.
summary: The voice in verse 1 speaks as Jesus Christ, the elders’ advocate who knows human weakness. It tells the elders who have not reached Zion that their mission is not yet full. Their testimony is recorded in heaven, angels rejoice over them, and their sins are forgiven. They are to continue to Zion, hold a meeting, rejoice, and offer a sacrament. Afterward they may return together or two by two, as long as they are faithful. Those who wish may ride horses, mules, or carriages if they receive this with thanks. These matters are left to their judgment and the Spirit. The revelation ends: “I am with the faithful always.”

contextNote.title: Credit before arrival
contextNote.text: These elders had preached their way west and had not yet reached Zion. Verse 2 says their mission is not yet full. Verse 3 explains why they are blessed anyway: their testimony is “recorded in heaven.” Angels look on it and rejoice, and their sins are forgiven. Verse 6 adds the purpose of the meeting: the faithful are brought together to rejoice in Missouri. In this passage, the heavenly record means their preaching already counts before the journey ends.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 60–63 draws its title from verse 9. Which choices in verses 5–8 does the Lord leave to the elders’ judgment, and what condition does verse 7 attach?
reviewNote: Read all 9 verses. Official heading gives the Missouri River bank at Chariton, 13 August 1831, after meeting elders bound for Zion. JSP historical introduction named Hyrum Smith, John Murdock, David Whitmer, and Harvey Whitlock and Murdock’s illness. Whitlock is not in people-ids and is not named in the text, so he was not added. The text says “chariots”; the summary paraphrases as carriages. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
